title: Dangerous Escalation in the Middle East: U.S.–Israel Strikes on Iran and Iran’s Retaliation Heighten the Risk of Regional War and Global Instability
author: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan

heroImage.caption: Rising tensions in the Middle East following U.S.–Israel and Iran military exchanges

inlineImage.caption: Calls for diplomacy amid escalating regional conflict

body.text: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson of the United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP), expressed profound concern over the rapidly deteriorating security situation in the Middle East, warning that the latest military escalation carries grave implications for regional and global peace.

He noted that the coordinated strikes conducted by the United States and Israel against Iranian targets on 28 February 2026 have triggered a dangerous cycle of retaliation. Iran’s subsequent missile and drone attacks on Israel and on U.S. forces and installations across the region have dramatically intensified tensions, raising the specter of a broader confrontation.

Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan emphasized that when states engage in cross‑border airstrikes, missile exchanges, and military mobilization—while drawing in their respective allies—the risk of miscalculation and uncontrolled escalation increases exponentially. Such dynamics can rapidly transform a regional crisis into a conflict involving major global powers, creating conditions that could spiral toward a catastrophic world war.

He stressed that war brings devastation on a scale that no nation can afford. Large‑scale conflict would result in massive loss of life, widespread displacement, and the collapse of essential infrastructure. Global trade routes, energy supplies, and critical economic systems would face severe disruption, affecting not only the Middle East but every region of the world.

Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan underscored that civilians—especially women, children, the elderly, and marginalized communities—bear the heaviest burden of war. Rising food and fuel prices, destroyed homes, shattered health systems, and long‑term psychological trauma become the enduring legacy of armed conflict.

He reminded the international community that history has repeatedly shown how localized violence can spill across borders with alarming speed. In such volatile circumstances, responsible leadership demands restraint, dialogue, and a commitment to peaceful resolution rather than further militarization.

Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan urged all parties to step back from the brink, prioritize diplomacy, and engage in meaningful negotiations. “We must give peace a chance,” he stated. “The world cannot afford another devastating war. Nations must choose diplomacy over confrontation and uphold their responsibility to protect human life, regional stability, and global peace.”
